SOURCE: MedGemma 1.5 Technical Report. Sellergren (co-first), Gao (co-first), Mahvar et al.; Google Research and Google DeepMind. arXiv:2604.05081v2, dated 2026-5-5 (v2 1 May 2026). Preprint, 2026.
COVERAGE: 64,123 of 64,123 chars; all 23 pages, including appendices A (CT-RATE, non-medical benchmark) and B (prompts). References skimmed. Text extraction is clean except table layout, where some adjacent numbers run together (noted below).

CLAIMS (ranked)
- claim: A single 4B model, MedGemma 1.5, handles 3D CT/MRI, whole-slide pathology, bounding-box localization, multi-timepoint CXR and lab-report extraction. It reuses the Gemma 3 architecture and the 400M MedSigLIP encoder, with no architectural change.
  number: none
  setup: 4B, Gemma 3 base, MedSigLIP vision encoder
  quote: "MedGemma 4B 1.5 is based off of Gemma3 (Team et al., 2025) with the same architecture. The vision encoder is 400M MedSigLIP encoder"
  where: p.2
- claim: 3D volumes are handled by slicing into 2D axial images, capped at 85 slices (21,760 vision tokens) so the total stays under 32K tokens.
  number: 85 slices, 21,760 tokens, 896x896
  setup: CT/MRI; slices sampled equidistantly along z if more than 85; slice indices interleaved in the prompt ("SLICE {index}")
  quote: "We capped the number of axial slices per query to a maximum of 85 during training and evaluation (which amount to 21,760 vision tokens), to stay below a total of 32K tokens"
  where: p.4 (Sec 2.3.1)
- claim: CT uses 3-channel windowing, with the red channel (-1024,1024), green (-135,215) and blue (0,80) HU windows. MRI has no windowing; each volume is min-max normalized with R=G=B.
  number: none
  setup: encoder trained on 256 intensity values per channel
  quote: "Red Channel (-1024, 1024)" / "Green Channel (-135, 215)" / "Blue Channel (0, 80)"
  where: p.5
- claim: WSI is handled by tissue-masked patch sampling. One magnification per slide is chosen at random (5x, 10x or 20x), the patches are 896x896, and they are capped at 126 per slide (32,256 tokens). Spatial order is kept.
  number: 126 patches, 32,256 tokens
  setup: P(5x)=0.34, P(10x)=0.33, P(20x)=0.33; random subsampling without replacement; the cap is higher than for CT because the captions are shorter
  quote: "we enforced a cap of 126 patches per slide (leading to 32256 vision tokens) via random subsampling without replacement"
  where: p.5-6
- claim: Training recipe. The vision encoder is frozen. The LLM gets continued pretraining, then distillation and RL as in Gemma 3. Extra domain-specific teachers are trained on CT, MRI and histopathology. WSI RL uses token-level ROUGE-L as the reward.
  number: distillation samples 256 teacher logits per token
  setup: Table 1 data includes CXR-IND1 605,732, CT Dataset 1 282,963, MRI Dataset 1 167,674, internal WSI 335,825, Chest ImaGenome 39,968 (RL only)
  quote: "Distillation here means we sample 256 teacher model logits per token, weighted by teacher probabilities."
  where: p.3-4
- claim: Headline gains over MedGemma 1 4B on the new tasks (Table 4).
  number: 3D MRI 51.3 to 64.7 (+11 points in abstract). CT 58.2 to 61.1. WSI ROUGE-L 2.2 to 49.4. ImaGenome IoU 3.1 to 38.0. MS-CXR-T macro-acc 61.1 to 65.7. In the extracted text, MRI reads "51.364.757.4" (51.3 and 64.7 are MG1 and MG1.5; 57.4 is the 27B). The text calls the MRI gain 11 points, so 64.7 may be a misparse; check the PDF page. Treat 64.7 as unverified.
  setup: internal CT Dataset 1 and MRI Dataset 1 (class-balanced, binary yes/no per condition, macro accuracy); temperature 0, single run
  quote: "improving 3D MRI condition classification accuracy by 11% and 3D CT condition classification by 3% (absolute improvements). In whole slide pathology imaging, MedGemma 1.5 4B achieves a 47% macro F1 gain." Table: "WSI Histopath ROUGE-L 2.249.44.1 ? 2.3 3.2 13.912.2 49.8(4)"
  where: abstract p.1; Table 4 p.7
  caveat: "47% macro F1" in the abstract is a ROUGE-L gain (2.2 to 49.4, which is +47.2 points), not F1. The abstract also says "4% macro accuracy" for MS-CXR-T, while Table 4 shows 61.1 to 65.7 (+4.6).
- claim: The 4B WSI result is roughly on par with the specialist PolyPath (49.8 ROUGE-L) and far above Gemini 3 Flash (13.9) and Pro (12.2). On localization the 4B model matches Gemini 3 Flash and Pro.
  number: ImaGenome mean IoU 38.0 (MG1.5) vs 38.5 (Flash) vs 39.1 (Pro) vs 30.7-34.4 (CoCa-CXR). Extraction reads "3.138.016.0 8.7 5.7 8.1 38.539.1", so the 27B value is 16.0.
  setup: prompt asks for JSON boxes [y0,x0,y1,x1] normalized to 0-1
  quote: "Chest ImaGenome (Localization) Mean IoU 3.138.016.0 8.7 5.7 8.1 38.539.1 30.7-34.4 (2)"
  where: Table 4 p.7
- claim: Lab-report extraction improves on three of the four datasets, and the Mendeley result is unchanged.
  number: EHR2 macro F1 78 to 91; EHR3 50 to 71; EHR4 25 to 64 (extraction reads "25645", so 64 then 5 for the 27B, which is uncertain); Mendeley 85 to 85. Task is JSON extraction (name, result, unit, specimen, method, collection time).
  setup: internal datasets, pathology lab tests only; PDFs rendered to images; Mendeley has only 14 images
  quote: "EHR Dataset 2 Macro F1 78 91 76 - 8493 9293 -"
  where: Table 4 p.7; Sec 3.2.5 p.10
  caveat: the abstract's "average of 18% macro F1" is actually the average gain, which does not match the table cleanly.
- claim: Text and EHR gains. MedQA 64.4 to 69.1. EHRQA 67.6 to 89.6 (the 27B scores 90.5). MedXpertQA multimodal 18.8 to 26.4. EHRNoteQA 79.4 to 80.4.
  number: as stated
  setup: thinking enabled by appending "SYSTEM INSTRUCTION: think silently if needed." for MedQA, MedMCQA, EHRNoteQA, PubMedQA, MMLU Med, MedXpertQA text and AfriMed-QA; temperature 0.0
  quote: "MedQA (4-op) (Jin et al., 2021) Accuracy 64.4 69.185.376.8 94.395.1" and "EHRQA Accuracy 67.6 89.690.587.3 94.995.2"
  where: Table 3 p.6
- claim: The model beats Qwen3 VL 4B on all vision tasks but loses on general text biomedical knowledge such as MedQA (76.8 vs 69.1).
  number: none beyond the table
  setup: some comparisons were not run for Qwen3 for "logistical constraints"
  quote: "Qwen3 VL 4B demonstrates superior performance on general text-based biomedical knowledge tasks, such as MedQA. However, MedGemma 1.5 significantly outperforms Qwen3 VL 4B in specialized clinical vision tasks"
  where: p.11
- claim: On out-of-distribution CT-RATE, MedGemma 4B models far outscore Gemini 3 Flash.
  number: macro F1 23.5 (MG1), 26.9 (MG1.5), 8.5 (Gemini 3 Flash)
  setup: public CT-RATE validation split, 18 conditions queried separately (18 queries per study), F1 because the labels are imbalanced
  quote: "CT-RATE∗ (3D CT) Macro F1 23.5 26.9 8.5"
  where: Table 5 p.19
- claim: Adding capabilities cost general knowledge. MMLU-Pro fell 39.1 to 33.8 (Gemma 3 4B scores 43.6).
  number: 39.1 to 33.8
  setup: non-medical text benchmark, 4B
  quote: "Table 6 shows a degradation in general knowledge reasoning compared to both its predecessor, MedGemma 1 4B and the foundational Gemma 3 4B."
  where: Appendix A p.19
- claim: Other regressions vs MedGemma 1 on 2D tasks.
  number: SlakeVQA 72.3 to 59.8; VQA-RAD 49.9 to 48.1; PubMedQA 73.4 to 67.6; CXR14 50.1 to 48.4; MMLU Med 70.0 to 69.7
  setup: Table 3
  quote: "SlakeVQA (Liu et al., 2021) Tokenized F1 72.359.8 70.3 53.5 62.562.8"
  where: Table 3 p.6
- claim: Other 2D gains. EyePACS accuracy 64.9 to 76.8. MIMIC-CXR RadGraph F1 21.9 to 27.2.
  number: as stated
  setup: Table 3
  quote: "EyePACS (Cuadros and Bresnick, 2009) Accuracy 64.9 76.875.3 41.9 66.963.4"
  where: p.6

LIMITS
- The authors concede regressions on SLAKE and VQA-RAD. They attribute these to benchmark quality: token-overlap scoring and non-standardized ground truth. They say targeted fine-tuning can bridge the gaps.
- The authors say the model is "not meant to be deployed without the necessary clinical fine-tuning". They say the capabilities are "foundational data processing tools, distinct from automated clinical decision-making".
- 3D CT/MRI and WSI evaluations use internal, non-public datasets (CT Dataset 1, MRI Dataset 1, WSI Histopath, EHR 2-4), so they cannot be reproduced. Only CT-RATE, MS-CXR-T and ImaGenome are public.
- CT/MRI labels come from regex plus Gemini extraction of reports, with manual review of a random subset only. A condition counts as absent if the report omits it. The sets were balanced by sub-sampling.
- Every evaluation is a single run at temperature 0.0, chosen on informal tune-set measurements. Other models use default temperature and top-k. The authors say prompts significantly affect results and that the prompts were hand-tuned for MedGemma 1.5 on train/validation splits.
- Internal CT/MRI/WSI test sets were held out from training, but the paper gives no per-dataset confidence intervals.
- MS-CXR-T: temporal mentions were removed from the pretraining reports.
- CT slices are limited to 85, so coverage of a volume is sparse. WSI is limited to 126 patches, which are randomly subsampled. Only single WSI-text pairs were evaluated.
- Some Qwen3 VL 4B evaluations are missing (WSI shows "?").
- Parts of the manuscript were drafted with Gemini 2.5 Pro and Gemini 3 Pro and then human-edited.
- Dated: the baselines are Gemini 3 Flash/Pro, Qwen3 VL 4B and Gemma 3. The report notes Qwen3 VL was "released about half a year after Gemma 3".

BUILDS ON
- Sellergren et al. 2025, MedGemma technical report (arXiv:2507.05201)
- Gemma Team 2025, Gemma 3 technical report (distillation and RL recipe)
- Zhai et al. 2023, SigLIP
- Yang et al. 2024, Med-Gemini
- Ahmed et al. 2025, PolyPath (WSI tissue segmentation, ROUGE-L evaluation, and the 49.8 external SOTA)
- Bannur et al. 2023 (MS-CXR-T, BioViL-T)
- Chen et al. 2025 (CoCa-CXR)
- Wu et al. 2021 (Chest ImaGenome)
- Hamamci et al. 2024 (CT-RATE)
- Kweon et al. 2024 (EHRNoteQA)
- Walonoski et al. 2018 (Synthea, for EHRQA)

CODE
- Localization prompt and format, from p.10: output a JSON list of objects with a label and box "[y0, x0, y1, x1]", normalized to [0,1], (y0,x0) top-left. Prompt is "{{ image }} + Where is the {object}?" (Table 12, p.22).
- CT prompt, from p.23: "{{ images }} + After looking at the indication and patient history "{HISTORY}"... Is there "{Label}" in the CT volume? You may write out your argument before stating your final answer "Final Answer: yes" or "Final Answer: no"."
- Thinking toggle, from p.20: append "SYSTEM INSTRUCTION: think silently if needed." to the system prompt. MedGemma has no native system prompt; baselines get "You are a helpful radiology assistant." or "You are a helpful medical assistant."
- Lab extraction prompt, from p.22 (Table 11): "You are a Clinical Data Extraction Specialist... extract all lab tests into a JSON list. Each test object ... name, result, unit, range, panel, method, specimen, sample_collection_time (formatted as DD-MM-YYYY HH:MM:SS)"

FIGURES (not extracted via the script; read from the text)
- Fig 1, p.2: collection overview. 27B text and multimodal, 1.5 4B new, MedSigLIP 0.4B encoder.
- Fig 2, p.3: bar chart of MG1 vs MG1.5 across medical text and imaging tasks, with the macro-average definition of "medical image interpretation" over 7 tasks. Useful as a summary.
- Fig 3, p.8: example CT liver-tumor prompt and response, with a radiologist review. The radiologist agreed on the tumor but disagreed on biliary dilation, which is a hallucination example.

PROBLEMS
- Table 3 and 4 columns are concatenated in the extraction (for example "69.185.376.8"), so a few cells are ambiguous. I flagged the MRI 64.7 and EHR4 64 values for a check against the PDF page.
- The abstract's "47% macro F1" for WSI and "18% macro F1" for lab reports do not match the tables' metrics (ROUGE-L, and per-dataset F1). The abstract's MRI "11%" matches the table only if MG1.5 is 64.7 vs 51.3 (+13.4), which it does not. The correct MRI gain is therefore uncertain.
- No embedded instructions in the text.
